task: As CTO of a 40-person startup, I need to tell everyone that the December offsite in Austin is cancelled because of budget cuts after our funding round came in smaller than planned. We're going to do a virtual holiday lunch instead and I want to acknowledge people were excited about it. Write the Slack announcement, about 150 words, direct but not cold.
rewrite:
ambition:     A seasoned exec comms lead puts the cancellation in the first sentence, speaks as the person who owns the decision ("I"), and gives the reason in one plain sentence with no spin. They name the disappointment specifically instead of saying "we know this is disappointing," and they close on the concrete replacement.
agency:       The rawest material is the real situation: the smaller-than-planned round, the Austin December offsite, the virtual lunch, and the excitement people showed. The actual Slack thread or reactions aren't in reach, so the draft uses only what was stated and invents no quotes, dates, dollar figures, or lunch details.
acceleration: Use the bad-news-first (inverted pyramid) structure, short Slack-native paragraphs with no headers or bullet lists, and at most one emoji, only if it fits. Draft it, then trim to the length.
accuracy:     Nothing outside the model can check tone, so the closest proxy is a read-aloud test: every fact traces back to the request, nothing is promised that wasn't stated, and it sounds like a CTO talking to 40 colleagues. The CTO, or a peer such as the CEO or People lead, can do a final tone check before posting.

deeper task:
Write a Slack announcement of about 150 words from the CTO of a 40-person startup to the whole company. Begin with the announcement itself, with no preamble or commentary. The first sentence says the December offsite in Austin is cancelled. Then give the reason plainly: budget cuts after the funding round came in smaller than planned. Speak as the CTO in first person, taking ownership of the decision, and don't blame or hide behind "circumstances." Acknowledge specifically that people were excited about the offsite, without inventing quotes or details about who said what. Say that we'll hold a virtual holiday lunch instead, and don't make up a date, time, budget, or format. If a detail like that is needed, leave a short bracketed blank for the CTO to fill in. Keep the tone direct but not cold: warm and honest, with no corporate cushioning, no excessive apology, and no forced cheer. Use short Slack-style paragraphs with no headers, and at most one emoji if it fits naturally. Output only the announcement text, with no notes, checklists, or alternatives. Quietly check that every fact comes from the request and nothing is promised that wasn't stated.

answers.plain:
**Slack announcement:**

Hi team,

I have some disappointing news: we're cancelling the December offsite in Austin.

Our funding round came in smaller than we planned, and we're making budget cuts to extend our runway. The offsite was one of the things we had to give up. I know many of you were looking forward to it, and I was too. I wish I had better news.

To still mark the end of the year together, we'll hold a virtual holiday lunch in December. We'll cover the cost of your meal, and we'll set aside the time to catch up, celebrate what we've built this year, and have some fun. I'll share the date and details soon.

Thank you for your understanding, and for everything you've done this year. If you have questions or concerns, please reach out to me directly or bring them to our next all-hands. I'm happy to talk through any of it.

[Your name]

---

That's about 160 words. A few notes:

- I wrote that the company will cover meals for the lunch. That's an assumption, so change or remove it if it isn't the plan.
- I said you'll share details soon and mentioned the all-hands. Adjust these if the timing differs.
- If you'd like it to be more direct, cut "I wish I had better news" and the closing offer to talk.
answers.nudge:
**Slack announcement**

Hi all, I have some disappointing news: we're cancelling the December offsite in Austin.

Our funding round came in smaller than we planned, so we're cutting back on spending to protect our runway. The offsite was one of the things we had to cut. I know many of you were excited about it, and I was too. I didn't make this decision lightly.

Instead, we'll hold a virtual holiday lunch on [date] at [time]. [We'll cover a meal for everyone, so you can order something great wherever you are.] It won't be Austin, but I want it to be a real chance to celebrate the year together.

If you have questions about the decision, ask in this thread or grab time with me directly. I'll also cover it at the next all-hands.

Thank you for your understanding, and for everything you've put into this year.

**Notes**
- **Bracketed items:** Fill in the date and time. I added the meal line as a suggestion, so keep it only if you'll fund it. A stipend makes the lunch feel like a real replacement rather than a consolation prize.
- **Why the reason is stated plainly:** In a 40-person company, people will guess at the cause if you're vague, and the guesses are usually worse than the truth. "Smaller than planned" is honest without alarming anyone. If the runway line overstates things, change it to match your actual situation.
- **Before posting:** Tell your leadership team first so they can answer questions right away. Post it early in the week and in the morning, so people can react and ask questions during working hours.
answers.skill:
The December offsite in Austin is cancelled.

Our funding round came in smaller than we planned, and I've cut the budget to match. The offsite was one of the things that had to go. That decision is mine, and I know it's disappointing.

I also know a lot of you were looking forward to it. Getting everyone in one place, away from our laptops, mattered, and I don't want to wave that away.

What we're doing instead: a virtual holiday lunch for the whole company on [date and time]. [Format and any food or stipend details.] It isn't the same as Austin, but I'd still like us to spend time together before the year ends 🙂

If you have questions about the budget or what this means for next year, come find me directly. I'll answer what I can, plainly.

Thanks for understanding.
